Subject: Follow-up: Reliability / SLO comparison + next tests

Jordan — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary from the call:
- Acme's top priority: predictable inference uptime and graceful failover across regions.
- You're evaluating Redwood vs Hyperscaler-managed endpoints for both latency and reliability under production burst traffic.
- Agreed: run a short, focused reliability test to validate failover behavior and how error budgets are consumed under sustained QPS.

Redwood competitive SLO highlights (high level):
- Default platform SLO: 99.95% regional uptime (we can support contractual SLAs on Dedicated).
- Rate-limiting behavior: adaptive queuing + shedding with clear 429 vs 5xx profiles; we expose error-budget metrics in Console.
- Failover: automated cross-region fallback (typical detection + failover < 30s for regional 5xx floods), plus customer-configurable fallback to smaller models to maintain latency.

Hyperscaler typical behavior we see in evaluations:
- High raw availability but throttling patterns differ (often hard 429s without graceful queuing).
- Failover can be slower if endpoints are zone-scoped; cross-region orchestration is possible but may require infra/config work.

Proposed tests (please confirm):
1) Sustained load: 5k QPS equivalent (50k tokens/s) for 30 minutes to observe error budget consumption and latency p95/p99 drift.
2) Failover drill: induce 5xx on primary region and confirm failover to backup region within 60s (target 30s).
3) Burst handling: 10x short bursts (1-2 min) to observe 429 vs queuing behavior and downstream retry/backoff impact.

Attachments: reliability_slo_summary.pdf (high-level comparison + suggested parameterization).

Next steps / asks from Acme:
- Can you confirm which test window works (Wed/Thu next week)?
- Provide a contact for network/infra coordination and an IP allowlist if required.

I'll share a short test plan doc and a small load harness script for review.

Thanks — Ben

Jordan — confirmed for Wed Apr 1, 08:00-11:30 PST. High-level runbook and responsibilities below plus links: 

Runbook (short):
- 07:30 PST: Redwood opens observation window (metrics + tracing dashboards shared).
- 08:00 PST: Sustained load start (Test #1) - 30 minutes at target QPS. Redwood will stream p95/p99 and error-rate dashboards to the shared Drive doc.
- 08:45 PST: Short cooldown, then start failover drill (Test #2) - we will simulate regional 5xx by returning controlled 5xx responses from a fronting proxy.
- 09:15 PST: Burst test (Test #3) - 10 short bursts, observe 429/queuing.
- 10:00 PST: Post-mortem window and live notes; capture error-budget delta and any incident classification.

Who owns what:
- Redwood (Ben/Marissa/Camila): run harness, provide Console links, capture error-budget metrics, provide a one-page post-test summary.
- Acme (Jordan + infra contact): provide IP allowlist & any internal monitoring observers, run Hyperscaler harness in parallel.
- Hyperscaler (Morgan): observe and provide their logs/metrics for comparison.

Answers to Jordan's questions (short):
- Error budget definition: we measure availability per-minute vs target SLO (99.95% default). Minutes with >2xx ratio below 99% are considered degraded for that minute; multiple degradation minutes count toward the error budget. Retries that succeed within our adaptive retry window are not counted as downtime, but retries that surface 5xx/429 to the client are considered failures.
- Historical uptime: attached is the 12-month hosted API rollup (redacted) - see the Drive link. Dedicated rollups vary by customer but typical contractual uptime is 99.98% for reserved pools; we can provide anonymized rollups.
- Failover triggers: primary signals are health-check misses and sustained >3% 5xx over a 1-minute window. We also trigger based on p99 latency breaches configurable per-customer.
